## Design

### 2026-10-18 – Hour 1 - Stand Angle

**10h**

Hour 1 - Stand Angle

I am a beginner at CAD, so I started with the easiest component to get the hang of it. I decided that instead of just 1 big scanner thing that is at an angle, it would be easier for prototyping and everything if I had the main scanner module and just a stand to hold it at an angle. This would make it easier to adjust the angle if necessary, as sometimes the scanners can be quite particular about how you hold the barcode up to it. For reference, the project is the same as the PCB week 1; now it's just the case for it. I started with a sketch; it was pretty simple. I played around with constraints vs. dimensions and figured out how to keep fewer dimensions and more constraints so I can easily edit stuff like the angle, and everything just changes with it.

![StandAngleThingSketch](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/5d0b5aeced8b4cd14003be1bfdc1e0d1723c8fd6de4e67c48fa3502f4ef78b43.png)

I then extruded it to what I thought would be the width of the case, based on the PCB and just some guessing.  (In retrospect, I had to adjust the width by a bit after making the actual case.)

![StandAngleThing](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/89137643a1ec0f69b92cf2bab52c274639af1e381a8acb6aeed4fe3a9786cf0c.png)

Hour 2 - Base

I worked on making the actual base or container that the components would sit in. Well, not directly. I decided that instead of screwing into the base, it would be easier if the PCB screws into the lid so there is space for the battery at the bottom of the base, and so then there can be extra space for wires and stuff underneath the PCB. And then when u take the lid off, u just unscrew the PCB from the lid, or if u just want to switch out the battery, you don't even need to unscrew the lid. (In retrospect, you would, cause u can't switch out the cable whose connector is on the front of the PCB, but that's fine.) I started with the sketch. I needed a way for the lid to screw into the case, so I decided on using M2 screws with heat-set inserts cause I have those already, and they're already being used for the PCB itself.

![BaseSketch](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/d93349cd30bdae1195b3a37709cd007bcef8472d09c2d571dba895e6947b8add.png)

I then extruded it up to what I thought would be the height of the base itself. I also cut out the space for the USB-C port and the power switch to sit in. Just guessing where they are going to be right now. The measurements for the base are from the PCB + some for tolerance, based on guesses.

![BaseV1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/e0f4dd982a44c422e517378f5eff1b799121f0b2c94fd1cf02f9693e897504eb.png)

Hour 3 - Lid

I started making the lid for the PCB. I used the dimensions of the base and stuff for how big it should be, and positioned the space for the holes in the same spot so they line up. I then had to guess where the holes for the scanner, the display, the LED, and the buzzer were going to be. I didn't have a concrete way to tell where the holes were going to be, so I was kind of just guessing where they were going to be. I didn't really know how to tell for sure, so at the time the plan was to just print it, see where the holes actually are, and update the CAD. Or just directly measure from the PCB when it gets here where the holes should be and update the CAD then. I spent a long time trying to figure out how to tell, but I kind of just gave up and guessed.

![LidSketchV2](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/96d2f92c152dce6d5218fc2f12300258ce85990b94e640309e085beca7193777.png)

I also added these legs for the PCB to attach to so that the components that sit up don't hit the lid, like the capacitor and stuff.

![LidV2](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/b3303e2e8ba8c68f6c9ad0b6a57e3fb34e7517b5a5197848d39e833c4c696895.png)

Hour 4, 5 & 6 - New Discovery

I found out while talking to a friend that you can actually export the PCB you make as a STEP file and import it into Fusion to work with it directly. This made it so much better because then I could directly check to see if the lid holes and things were in the right spot. It took me a bit because the actual screen CAD wasn't there, only the socket, so I had to find that on GrabCAD and figure out how to join them. I searched for the scanner but couldn't find it, so i just made sure the hole was the correct size, cause the scanner can actually be placed anywhere since its wires plug into a socket. Then when I went to assemble it with the lid, the actual PCB kept moving away from the components. So it took me a while to figure out how to fix that by making it all a rigid group (I had to learn what that is). Then I had to update the Lid, a lot. Basically, all the holes were in the wrong place, but I used the measure tool to look at how much each thing needed to be moved and updated the sketch from that; ofc I was wrong quite a few times. And all the sizes for stuff were off, so that had to be adjusted as well.

![LidSketch](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/f9c1a2b834b6ee52b14f9cce581dda2f2d4456b10fe819631129a83cdbdba0b9.png)

![CheckingFitsForHeights](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/fbc0773b095ac867cae6901048526c4d32e0b936996029ea5834a77c02655fff.png)

The model at the bottom is the placeholder model for the battery.

Hour 7 & 8 - Assembly

I worked on assembling everything together. It started off really rough, as I had to figure out how assemblies work, and I kept bringing things into each other's assemblies and almost created many circular references and stuff. Then I finally figured out how to assemble it all together I obviously had to make changes to make sure the base fit the lid, and the PCB components weren't phasing through the bottom or the sides (they were on multiple occasions). It took a lot of changing heights and widths and stuff to make sure everything fit, and then I brought in the stand for the back, which also had to be adjusted for the length of the scanner module and the width of the scanner module.

![UnfinishedAssembly](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/87794d430abdac2b05570c4de96bd612014d42895b1ddadd65bf0320b8188a11.png)

![SlightlyLessUnfinishedAssembly](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Gh41LCklf8pAFUOLAd0zqSVIN2Jmcw6K/a44f62cc7b996776453964457d4898ba76c9907813e83547b540c2bc1a4def24.png)

Hour 9 & 10 - Fillets and Chamfers

I was told by a friend that having fillets and chamfers makes the product print better in 3D and makes it a more finished product. So I spent a lot of time playing around with those tools to figure out the best configuration and values for those; it was mostly just a guessing game and seeing if it worked out.
